params.description: Parameter sets this tenant reads, per role: `{tenant: tenant-initech}`, or a list per role merged in order. Any document of the extends chain may name sets: per role they merge root first, leaf last, later winning per leaf key. `${param:<role>.<key>}` in the spec of any document of the chain reads the merged values.

name_rule.description: The name every tenant built on this one must have, with `${param:<role>.<key>}` tokens filled from that tenant's parameter sets (`${param:tenant.code}`). Only `${param:}` tokens are allowed.

tags.description: Optional tags (list of values for categorization)

TenantSpecModel.description:
A customer or organisation: its display name, the data-residency geographies it may deploy into, and defaults (`environments`, `properties`, `custom`) that every deployment for it inherits.

Rules:
- Geographies must be unique.
- Environment references must be unique, because a repeat would merge twice.
- A tenant needs `display_name`. A `partial: true` tenant, or one with `extends`, is exempt because its missing fields come from the base.

partial.description: When true this is a base for other tenants (`extends`), not a tenant of its own: `display_name` may be absent, no deployment may name it in `tenant`, and no `${value:}` token may read it.

extends.description: Name of a base Tenant whose spec is merged into this one when the solution loads. Child always wins: `display_name` and `onboarded` are replaced, `geographies` is replaced by the child's list when it sets one, `environments` is the base's list then the child's, and `properties`, `custom` and `configuration` deep-merge per leaf key. Circular chains are rejected.

display_name.description: Human-readable tenant name (e.g. 'Acme Corporation'). The tenant's identifier/code is meta.name (e.g. 'contoso'). Required, unless the tenant is `partial` or gets it through `extends`.

geographies.description: Data-residency boundaries this tenant may deploy into, for example `europe`. Each must be the `geography` of some region in a ProviderConfig. A deployment for this tenant is flagged when its provider's region lies in a geography that is not listed here. Omit for no restriction.

onboarded.description: ISO date the tenant was onboarded (e.g. 2026-03-15). Informational only.

environments.description: Names of Environment documents that merge before the deployment's own environments, so the deployment's values win. Use for tenant-wide defaults such as shared variables or feature flags.

properties.description: Tenant-wide properties, merged as the base layer into the `properties` of every deployment for this tenant. Deployment values win.

configuration.description: Tenant-specific settings, for example a CRM id or billing code, passed to Terraform as `strata.tenant.configuration`. Not merged into the deployment's properties. Add an `attributeconfig` with `target.kind: tenant` and `target.block: configuration` to validate them.

custom.description: Tenant-wide custom values, merged as the base layer into the `custom` values of every deployment for this tenant. Deployment values win.

ParamToken.description: Filled from the document's parameter sets when the solution loads (`${param:<role>.<key>}`).

description:
A customer or organisation identity. `meta.name` is the tenant code, for example `contoso`. Create one per customer and reference it from a deployment's `tenant`. Typically one per customer directory.

Rules:
- A tenant cannot extend itself; longer extends cycles are rejected when the solution loads.

spec.description:
Tenant specification (identity, geographies, environments, defaults)

Rules:
- Geographies must be unique.
- Environment references must be unique, because a repeat would merge twice.
- A tenant needs `display_name`. A `partial: true` tenant, or one with `extends`, is exempt because its missing fields come from the base.
